1

Due date calendar: two months, filling the box, inside the window

approved

APPROVED — goes live when you say so

Where: the Edit window → Due Date → press the date field.

"In the edit section, in the due date, you made the calendar thin. It needs to be the width of the box that it's in. Matter of fact, the box that it's in has to be inside the edit thingy box."

now

The Due Date was a plain text field (ringed red below). The calendar it opened was the browser's own, drawn outside the page — which is exactly why the app could neither widen it nor keep it inside the window.

after

Two months side by side, filling 78% of the window width, and measured to sit entirely inside the Edit window on all four sides. Today and Tomorrow sit on top.

what was really wrong

This was not a styling problem. The field was <input type="date">, so Chrome drew the calendar itself, outside the page. Every other date control in your planner already uses the app's own picker — the reminder clock, the tree chips, the reschedule picker. This one now does too, so there is one picker in five places rather than two that drift apart.

Measured after the change: picker 449px wide inside a 575px window, right edge 6px inside the window instead of 147px outside it.

2

Focus SESSION — I built the wrong feature, and I have taken it back out

not approved

NOT APPROVED — I built the wrong thing

Where: Focus sessions — the time band on the calendar, not the blue Focus mode button.

"Your showing focus mode, I am talking about focus session, don't get confused and go over it again. 2 is not approved as of now."

now

Your planner has two different things with similar names. Focus mode is the blue button that narrows the priority tree to one branch. A focus session is a time band on the calendar with a branch attached to it.

after

I made a focus session filter the priority tree — which is focus mode's job. That change is removed. Nothing about focus sessions has changed in your planner.

what I got wrong

You said "whatever is selected there would be the only thing showing on the calendar" and I read it as the priority tree. A focus session owns a stretch of the day, so its branch box should govern what shows on the calendar during that band - not what the tree lists. The two pictures above show the mistake: that is focus mode's behaviour, not a session's.

before I try again, one question

When a focus session runs from 9 to 11 and you pick Taxes in it, what should happen?

(a) during 9-11 the calendar shows only Taxes items, and the rest of the day is normal
(b) the whole calendar shows only Taxes for as long as that session is on
(c) something else - tell me in your words

I would rather ask than build the wrong thing a second time.

Where: the priority tree → Deleted.

now

and double click opens this

what I checked

The pen shows only on rows that really have notes. In the AFTER picture "Scan the receipts" has none, because it has no notes — a mark that appeared on everything would tell you nothing. Notes that are only spaces do not count either.

You chose the read-only view over the full Edit window, so you can read a deleted task without editing something that is sitting in the trash. Restore is right there on it.

brighter, on the deleted section only

You asked for the pen to be really more bright on the delete section only. Measured: it is now 3.4 times brighter than before (full-strength amber with a soft glow, 15px instead of 13px).
